title: The Mystery Islands
acts: The pleasure cruiser Marmalade went down in four feet of water, which is the least dignified depth available, and deposited its entire passenger manifest across five islands like a dropped tray of canapés. By the second morning Desert Island had organised itself, badly. Ayla stood at the tideline in her good hoop earrings, negotiating with a dorsal fin that was patrolling her stretch of water, offering it one earring now and one on delivery. Bastian — the only man on that blazing spit of sand, and pinned neatly between two cacti — had discovered that a cactus contains water and that a cactus objects to this being discussed, and was extracting it drop by drop through a lifejacket buckle without once removing his sunglasses. Emma had abandoned rescue entirely in favour of a sandcastle, currently a nine-tenths-scale Marmalade with a working funnel. Up on the high northeast dune Denise flashed a compact mirror at an aeroplane that was, on closer inspection, a gull. And Helena had simply walked into the island's one shabby house, claimed it, and begun sweeping, on the grounds that somebody had to have standards and there wasn't a cactus for miles.

Town Island had houses, which meant Town Island had politics. Fred planted himself on the southernmost doorstep in the settlement and declared himself Mayor of the South, waxing his moustache with factor 50 to look the part. Nikita worked north to south through the empty kitchens, liberating tinned peaches and a pair of enormous sunglasses she insisted had always been hers. Above her, at the town's north waterline, Irene fended off a cruising fin with a broken oar while shouting a full inventory of the tinned peaches southward to Nikita, who could not hear a word. Lyra, meanwhile, had located the island's single tree, arranged herself beneath it, and declined to participate in the emergency in any capacity. Far away across the water, on the loneliest scrap of land in the archipelago, Vincent was pacing his shore with a pencil and a piece of driftwood, drawing up the Official Rescue Rankings — who would be picked up first, second, and (he had underlined this twice) last. Vincent had awarded himself the best island. Vincent was not, it turned out, going to be picked up at all.

On Forest Island the survivalism reached its peak and stayed there. Kent had found the cabin, barricaded the door, and was conducting a solemn inventory of three biscuits, which is exactly as long an inventory as it sounds. Six rows south of him at the forest's sandy hem, Graham knelt in the sand rubbing two sticks together with tremendous conviction and no fire, his beard by now a genuine hazard. Far to the northeast, Joseph stood in the sand beside a tree, shaking it with the grim patience of a man who has been told trees contain food and intends to hold the tree to that. Out in the open sea, two people had elected not to make landfall at all. Olivia trod water with great composure, counting the heads south of her — exactly two, she noted, which meant her rescue position was better than people appreciated. East of her, Cassius floated on his back beside a lazily circling shark, spectacles fogged, explaining to it in his best courtroom voice the maritime law of salvage and who, precisely, it would be hearing from. And somewhere beyond all of them, a young tree was being bent slowly backwards.

whereabouts.A: Ayla was down at the Desert Island waterline in her hoop earrings, brokering safe passage with the shark patrolling her row, one earring up front and one on arrival.
whereabouts.B: Bastian, wedged between his two cacti and refusing to take his sunglasses off, was tapping them for water with a lifejacket buckle and losing the argument.
whereabouts.C: Cassius floated on his back out in the open sea east of Olivia, spectacles fogged, reading the maritime law of salvage aloud to a shark that had drifted alongside him.
whereabouts.D: Denise stood on the high northeast dune above Ayla, flashing a compact mirror at what she was certain was a rescue plane and was in fact a gull.
whereabouts.E: Emma sat on the sand building a nine-tenths-scale replica of the sunken Marmalade, complete with funnel, and would not be interrupted for anything as minor as rescue.
whereabouts.F: Fred occupied the southernmost doorstep on Town Island, having appointed himself Mayor of the South and waxed his moustache with sun cream for the ceremony.
whereabouts.G: Graham knelt in the sand at the forest's edge, six rows south of Joseph, rubbing two sticks together with total conviction and producing warm sticks.
whereabouts.H: Helena had claimed the desert's one house — not a cactus in reach, as she pointed out — and was sweeping it out while telling Denise the dune was no place for a signal station.
whereabouts.I: Irene stood at the town's north waterline poking a dorsal fin away with a broken oar while shouting a tinned-peach inventory south to Nikita, who could not hear her.
whereabouts.J: Joseph stood in the sand beside a forest tree well east of Lyra, shaking it steadily on the theory that trees contain food and this one was simply being difficult.
whereabouts.K: Kent had barricaded himself inside the forest cabin — the only person on the whole archipelago with a roof he'd chosen — and was formally inventorying three biscuits.
whereabouts.L: Lyra had claimed the shade of Town Island's only tree, sunglasses down, sunbathing through the emergency and declining every job the other three tried to give her.
whereabouts.M: Michael stood at the western tip of the loneliest island, a shark cruising the water down his column, quietly and thoughtfully bending a young springy tree backwards.
whereabouts.N: Nikita worked south from house to house through the abandoned town, liberating tinned peaches and a pair of enormous sunglasses she maintains were always hers.
whereabouts.O: Olivia trod water in the open sea west of Cassius, counting the two people south of her and declining rescue until it could be done in the correct order.
whereabouts.V: Vincent paced his lonely shore with a pencil and a plank, drafting the Official Rescue Rankings and awarding himself both the best island and first collection.

reveal: It was Michael, on Lonely Island — the only two people on it, and the killer was alone with the victim. Michael had spent the whole shipwreck reading the driftwood over Vincent's shoulder, and had discovered he was ranked last: below the sandcastle, below the biscuits, below the shark. So he did what any reasonable castaway would. He bent the young tree beside him all the way back to the sand, packed a whole shrub into it root-ball and all, sighted along the beach, and let go. The shrub crossed the island like a green cannonball with leaves trailing behind it, and Vincent went over like the last skittle in the frame — pencil up, plank up, rankings fluttering down over him in order. The tree, entirely unbothered, sprang back to vertical. Michael was on the far side of the island looking innocently at a shark by the time the driftwood landed.

escape.generic: The case was closed with a shrug and a rescue helicopter, everyone was handed a foil blanket and a biscuit, and the one person who actually did it stepped aboard, asked for a window seat, and slept the whole way home.

byAccused.A: Ayla was led off still trying to renegotiate — this time for a second earring back — while the person who really did it accepted a foil blanket and a second biscuit.
byAccused.B: Bastian was arrested in his sunglasses, which he declined to remove for the photograph, and the real culprit stood two rows behind him looking sunburnt and blameless.
byAccused.C: Cassius was fished out of the water and charged before he'd finished his sentence about salvage law, and the guilty party was quietly issued dry socks.
byAccused.D: Denise was taken away still insisting a plane had seen her, and the person who actually did it waved her off with the gull.
byAccused.E: Emma was arrested beside her sandcastle, which the tide took as she was walked to the boat, and the real killer helped carry her bucket.
byAccused.F: Fred's mayoralty ended with handcuffs and a firm speech about jurisdiction, and the person who really did it applauded politely from the dock.
byAccused.G: Graham was charged just as his sticks began to smoke, which he considers the true miscarriage of justice, while the guilty party borrowed his lighter on the boat home.
byAccused.H: Helena was arrested in a house so spotless the officers wiped their feet, and the real culprit complimented the floors on the way past.
byAccused.I: Irene was taken in mid-inventory, still holding the oar, and the person who actually did it kindly offered to carry the peaches.
byAccused.J: Joseph was hauled off mid-shake and the tree finally dropped its fruit thirty seconds later, by which time the real killer was already eating it.
byAccused.K: Kent had to be talked out of the cabin, biscuits and all, and the guilty party assured the officers through the door that he'd always seemed the type.
byAccused.L: Lyra was arrested without getting up, which she managed to make look like a lifestyle choice, and the real culprit obligingly moved into her patch of shade.
byAccused.N: Nikita went down for the peaches and the sunglasses both, and the person who actually did it kept the sunglasses.
byAccused.O: Olivia was taken into custody out of order, which she protested more loudly than the arrest itself, while the guilty party was rescued exactly on schedule.
